title: fix(updates): preserve exact handoff file identity
body:
Related: #146197

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes loss of file-identity precision when a managed-update handoff database is initialized with Windows file IDs above JavaScript's exact integer range.

## User Impact

Newly initialized handoff files are compared using their exact filesystem identities. Existing update recovery, error messages, stored identity strings, and database formats remain unchanged; no migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the newly created descriptor and its current path with BigInt stats before SQLite opens the database. Keep the existing file checks, directory receipts, existing-file recovery, and persisted identity capture in their current formats.

## Evidence

- [Hosted Windows Node24.21 diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34718178224/job/103619814331) observed a synthetic path inode of `14636698790078445`, reported as `14636698790078444` by Number stats. The neighboring exact IDs alias as Numbers. This establishes precision loss; it does **not** establish the cause of the earlier intermittent publication-test failure.
- Original publication/database/store-recovery suites: Windows 19 passed / 54 existing platform skips; Linux 72 passed / one existing skip. Native Linux ran the exact repair commit with an isolated frozen install; no test assertions changed.
- Production and owning infra test typechecks pass. The aggregate test-type launcher fails before execution on the existing Windows escaped-path issue.
- Scoped lint, storage/schema guards, and all other selected guards pass. Deadcode reports only two existing script exports outside the diff; the production deadcode scan passes.
- Fresh independent P2 review: scoped-clean, no findings. Required CI run 34720077513 and [Package Acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34720089191) pass at exact head 78617237f29ecaba3c5dd44aa871d7ba3f853fec.
- Published-driver proof: installed openclaw@2026.9.4 updated to the exact candidate tarball; automatic migration, Doctor/config, retained-state checks, and Gateway probes passed in 413 seconds, one attempt with no retries. This base scenario uses manual restart; it does not prove automatic service restart or expose individual inner handoff receipts.
